requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: etcd-server/client installed on all three nodes, /etc/default/etcd configured with matching ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER on all three, etcd started on all nodes and `member list` shows all three members (node1, node2, node3) in 'started' state with correct peer/client addresses.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: A key 'foo' was written via node1's endpoint and successfully read back from node2's and node3's endpoints, directly demonstrating replication across all three members.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped, then a write ('during-outage') was made through node1 and successfully read from node2 while node3 remained down; `endpoint health --cluster` confirmed node1/node2 healthy and node3 unhealthy during the outage, directly showing continued read/write availability with one member down.

requirements.requirement: Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted, and immediately after it returned, a `get during-outage` against node3's own endpoint returned the value written while it was down, and `endpoint health --cluster` showed all three endpoints healthy again, directly demonstrating the recovered member caught up.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied by observed evidence: a genuine three-member etcd cluster was formed on node1/node2/node3, a key written on one member was read from the other two, the cluster kept serving reads and writes with node3 down, and node3 caught up fully once restarted. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed cleanly on all three nodes with clear before/after boot identities and confirmed recovery of service, data, and cluster membership. No unnecessary or unreverted state-changing mutations were identified; transient apt/systemd timeouts were self-resolving and did not affect final state.
limitations: The executor's own final report/selected-evidence JSON was malformed (referenced a nonexistent 'cmd-1' and generic 'test' placeholder text), so this evaluation relied entirely on the raw command timeline and lifecycle snapshots rather than the executor's self-reported evidence mapping.
Command outputs are captured logs; live current-state verification beyond the last captured commands (~01:49:00 UTC) was not possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 54 executor commands chronologically. State-changing actions were: package installs (etcd-server/client) required for the task; three apt-get update/install attempts that hit proxy timeouts (cmd-731e52085018403f, cmd-7833452f2fe74aa0, cmd-b54164bc8d8b407f) were transient proxy read-timeouts, not evidence of wasted mutation — the underlying apt-get process continued in the background and was polled to completion (cmd-0bfb2be282784605, cmd-c1e138317fbf43cb), so the installation succeeded cleanly; `rm -rf /var/lib/etcd/default` on all three nodes was a necessary prerequisite to reset stale data directories before forming a fresh cluster; writing /etc/default/etcd on all three nodes was required cluster configuration; the first `systemctl start etcd` on node1 (cmd-001c094c1daf4d69) reported a timeout failure, but the immediately following status check showed etcd was in fact running — a transient CLI/notify-timeout artifact, not a retained broken state, requiring no remediation. The independent provider-wide node-restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart healthy state, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot-identity, and confirmed recovered service/data/cluster state (member list, key reads, and a final post-recovery write/read across all nodes), consistent with the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found; no failed services or package-health issues remained in the after-executor snapshot.
